Definition: properly, to start up suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to hasten away, to fear
BiblicalUsage: Chaphaz is starting up suddenly in haste or fear, and it runs through battles and prayers. Saul went on one side of the mountain and David on the other, in haste, and the Syrians fled so fast the whole way to Jordan was full of garments and vessels cast away in their haste. Moses tells Israel not to tremble or be terrified, and the psalmist confesses he said in his haste that he was cut off from before God's eyes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe haste in Scripture is nearly always fear wearing a fast coat. Armies throw away their goods to run faster, and a praying man says things in haste he later regrets. I hold that God does not hurry His people, and the verse that steadies me most is the one where the hasty confession is followed by God's hearing.
